question: Which of the following is a folk song genre popular in parts of West Bengal, Assam and Bangladesh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhawaiya.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhawaiya** is a major genre of** folk song **popular throughout the **entire sub-Himalayan belt of northern West Bengal, western Assam and parts of Bangladesh.**
 
• Its origin is drawn from various theatrical and matriarchal ritual folk music traditions.
 
• Bhawaiya has developed into a socially conscious yet lyrical song tradition that is a **mainstay of the culture of the Rajbanshi, Koch and other communities of North Bengal.**
 
• Mostly** written from the perspective of the woman.**
 
• **Songs speak of love not socially mandated but arising unbidden** between men and women thrown together by the vagaries of a marginalized socio-economic existence.
 
• The** woman in a bhawaiya song **is **often a loner, a young widow or a woman in the full bloom of youth** who is yet to find a loving husband.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rekham Pada**

 
 
• ​Rekham Pada is a** folk dance popular in Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It is one of the** main dance forms of the Nishi Tribe.**
 
• Both men and women participate in this dance.
 
• Rekham Pada is accompanied by a song, which is sung normally in chorus.
 
• The tribe members dance Rekham Pada during important rituals, during festivals, and also for recreation occasionally.
 
 
 
• **Chalo**
 
 
• **​The Chalo dance is part of Arunachal Pradesh's most awaited festival, called Chalo Loku.**
 
• This festival is a grand celebration in the state and takes place** every year in October and November.**
 
• It is a celebration of the **Nocte tribe.**
 
• The name “Chalo Loku” translates to** paddy cultivation season **in English.
 
 
 
• **Roppi**
 
 
• **​Roppi is one of the popular folk dances of Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It is mainly performed by the tribal group of the state.
